title: Optimization
opening: A learner can receive an incorrect comment sooner. That shortens delivery time, but does not establish whether the learner can correct the error.

labels.demo: Compare a goal with its proxy
labels.demoIntro: The example assumes that automated comments arrive sooner and are incorrect. No learner result is supplied, so the effect on the learner remains unknown.
labels.comparison: Compare a goal with its proxy
labels.comparisonIntro: The example assumes that automated comments arrive sooner and are incorrect. No learner result is supplied, so the effect on the learner remains unknown.
labels.goalGroup: Goal to judge the change against
labels.signalQuestion: Goal to judge the change against
labels.goalText: Judge change by whether the learner can correct the error.
labels.proxyText: Delivery time is a proxy; a faster comment does not show what the learner can do.
labels.resultUsefulFaster: Delivery time improves in the example. With the learner's correction as the goal, the result remains unknown: faster delivery alone does not show whether the learner corrected the error.
labels.resultSpeedFaster: The delivery-time proxy improves. Whether the learner corrected the error remains unknown; the proxy does not answer that question.
labels.resultUsefulMaintain: The example says the existing answer is adequate. Keeping it maintains the goal; a new change is not automatically an improvement.
labels.resultSpeedMaintain: No delivery-time comparison is given for the adequate answer. It may maintain usefulness, but there is not enough information to say it improves speed.
labels.resources: The example gives no resource use to compare. It cannot show whether the new arrangement uses resources better or increases what those resources can produce.
labels.loopTitle: The next change follows the evidence
labels.loopText: Name the goal, observe the present result, change a relevant part and compare what happens. The feedback chooses the next change. Reconsider the goal when new findings change what is worth pursuing.
labels.practice: Examine a goal you care about
labels.practiceIntro: Keep the goal, the number used as a proxy and the observed result in separate sentences. Include a condition that must remain intact.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.sampleLoaded: Authored example loaded. Replace it with your own evidence when useful.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: Optimization is iterative change based on feedback toward a goal. Name the goal, observe the present result, change a relevant part of the arrangement and compare what happens. Use that feedback to choose the next change. Effectiveness checks whether the goal is being met; efficiency and leverage compare the useful result with what it takes. Changing the goal changes what counts as an improvement.

example.goal: Useful feedback helps a learner correct an error.
example.current: The example assumes the existing answer is adequate. No measured performance is supplied.
example.proxy: Delivery time is a proxy. Sending an incorrect comment sooner improves that proxy, not the learning goal.
example.protected: The feedback must remain useful and correct enough to support the intended correction.
example.return: Compare an actual learner result under relevant conditions before claiming the change worked. If the goal is no longer worthwhile, reconsider it instead of optimizing the old process.
